results.title: The Use of Mixed-Methods Research in Social Sciences
results.content: # The Use of Mixed-Methods Research in Social Sciences. Social sciences, by their very nature, delve into the intricacies of human behavior, society, and culture. To capture the multifaceted realities of the social world, researchers often employ a combination of quantitative and qualitative research methods, a practice known as mixed-methods research. This approach allows for a more comprehensive exploration of complex social phenomena, offering deeper insights than either method alone can provide. # **The Synergy of Quantitative and Qualitative Methods**. In the realm of social sciences, the marriage of quantitative and qualitative research methods has proven to be a powerful approach. **Quantitative methods** are characterized by their systematic and structured approach to data collection and analysis. The synergy of quantitative and qualitative methods has become a hallmark of robust and comprehensive research in the social sciences. Mixed-methods research stands as a versatile and potent approach within the social sciences, offering a multitude of advantages that enrich the research process and deepen our understanding of complex phenomena.

results.title: [PDF] The Nature and Design of Mixed Methods Research - OBSSR
results.content: For purposes of this discussion, mixed methods research will be defined as a research approach or methodology: • focusing on research questions that call for real-life contextual understandings, multi-level perspectives, and cultural influences; • employing rigorous quantitative research assessing magnitude and frequency of constructs and rigorous qualitative research exploring the meaning and understanding of constructs; • utilizing multiple methods (e.g., intervention trials and in-depth interviews); • intentionally integrating or combining these methods to draw on the strengths of each; and • framing the investigation within philosophical and theoretical positions. ❖ ❖ The combination of quantitative and qualitative data: Mixed methods research begins with the assumption that investigators, in understanding the social and health worlds, gather evidence based on the nature of the question and theoretical orientation. ❖ ❖ The integration of multiple forms of data: In mixed methods studies, investigators intentionally integrate or combine quantitative and qualitative data rather than keeping them separate.
